why: no-confidence motion most powerful accountability tool, same as PYQ

q.x: The no-confidence motion is the most powerful weapon of accountability and need not state reasons; Question Hour is the most effective day-to-day vigil.

The **Speaker** has discretion to admit or reject a no-confidence motion.
Censure can be against a **minister or a group**; no-confidence only the **entire** Council.

**Simple closure** ends debate and puts the matter to vote; **point of order** is raised when proceedings depart from rules; **calling attention** seeks a minister's statement.

**Guillotine**: all pending clauses put to vote when time ends.
**Three-line whip** = strict voting direction.

Parliamentary system – executive responsible to the legislature

q.x: The 7th Amendment, 1956 added a proviso to Article 153 so that one person can be Governor of two or more States.

q.x: Reservation of Bills by the Governor for the President is a classic example of central control over the States.

o: Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha

q.s: In December 2020, the Andhra Pradesh High Court asked whether it could record a 'breakdown of constitutional machinery' in the State. Which Article of the Constitution does this relate to?
q.x: Breakdown of constitutional machinery in a State is the ground for President's Rule under Article 356.

q.s:
Assertion (A): Orders of the Delimitation Commission cannot be questioned in court.
Reason (R): Orders of the Delimitation Commission cannot be modified by legislatures.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
q.x: Both are true: Delimitation Commission orders cannot be challenged in court, and legislatures cannot change them. These are two separate safeguards, so R does not explain A.
q.tq: Ask whether two parallel safeguards explain each other.
n: Orders of the Delimitation Commission cannot be questioned in court. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Orders of the Delimitation Commission cannot be modified by legislatures. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.
A: **Delimitation Commission** orders **cannot be called in question** in **any court** (**Article 329**).
R: they **cannot be modified** by **Parliament** or **State Assemblies** — a separate safeguard.
xa: Orders have the **force of law**.
**Four** Commissions so far — **1952, 1963, 1973, 2002**.
⚠ **J.L. Kapur** chaired two (**1963, 1973**).

Match List-I (Finance Commission) with List-II (Chairman):

b. 11th | ii. K.C. Pant

q.x: 10th – K.C. Pant (1995-2000); 11th – A.M. Khusro (2000-05); 12th – C. Rangarajan (2005-10); 13th – Vijay Kelkar (2010-15).

q.s: Which one of the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India is NOT correct?
o: He is called the guardian of the public purse
He heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department
He controls the entire financial system of the country
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called him the most important officer under the Constitution
q.x: C is the incorrect statement (APPSC-G2 2017). The Indian CAG is only an Auditor-General: unlike the British C&AG, he has no control over the issue of money from the Consolidated Fund. A, B and D are all correct: he is called the guardian of the public purse, he heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department, and Ambedkar called him the most important officer under the Constitution.
q.tq: Indian CAG audits; he does not control the issue of money.
xs: "**He controls the entire financial system of the country**" is wrong — option **(3)** (**APPSC-G2 2017**).
He has **no control over the issue of money** from the Consolidated Fund — he is only an **Auditor-General**.
The rest are true: "**guardian of the public purse**", head of the **Indian Audit and Accounts Department**, and **Ambedkar's** "most important officer".
xa: In **Britain** the C&AG does control issue.
He is the PAC's "**friend, philosopher and guide**".

q.s: What did the democratic decentralisation recommended by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee essentially consist of?
q.x: The recommended remedy was democratic decentralisation through elected three-tier local bodies, which later came to be known as Panchayati Raj.
q.tq: Link the remedy proposed by the reviewing committee with its institutional form.
xs: Democratic decentralisation meant **three-tier elected local bodies** — option **(4)**.
Tiers: **Gram Panchayat** (village), **Panchayat Samiti** (block), **Zila Parishad** (district), "organically linked" by **indirect elections**.
xa: It meant genuine transfer of **power and responsibility** with **adequate resources**.
The scheme "later came to be known as **Panchayati Raj**".
⚠ **Nyaya Panchayat** is NOT one of the three tiers (UPPSC 2024).

q.s:
With reference to the three-tier model recommended by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee, consider the following statements:
1. Only the village panchayat was to be directly elected.
2. The Panchayat Samiti was to be an advisory body.
3. The District Collector was to be the chairman of the Zila Parishad.
4. The Zila Parishad was to be the executive body.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
q.x: Statements 2 and 4 are wrong: under BRM the Panchayat Samiti (block) was the executive body, while the Zila Parishad was an advisory, coordinating and supervisory body. Only the Gram Panchayat was directly elected (the upper tiers indirectly), and the Collector was to chair the Zila Parishad.

q.s: Which of the following statements regarding Nyaya Panchayats is correct?
o: The L.M. Singhvi Committee rejected Nyaya Panchayats for village clusters
The G.V.K. Rao Committee recommended Nyaya Panchayats as the executive arm of the Zila Parishad
The Ashok Mehta Committee recommended Nyaya Panchayats as separate bodies under a qualified judge
The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee included Nyaya Panchayat as one of the three tiers
q.x: The Ashok Mehta Committee recommended Nyaya Panchayats as separate bodies under a qualified judge. Nyaya Panchayat was not one of the three tiers recommended by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee; L.M. Singhvi also supported Nyaya Panchayats for clusters of villages.
q.tq: Distinguish a separate judicial body from the three administrative tiers of Panchayati Raj.
xs: The **Ashok Mehta Committee** wanted Nyaya Panchayats **separate from development panchayats**, under a **qualified judge** — option **(3)**.
**L.M. Singhvi** **supported** Nyaya Panchayats for **clusters of villages**, so option 1 is false.
Nyaya Panchayat was **not** one of the **Balwant Rai Mehta** three tiers (UPPSC 2024).
xa: Nyaya Panchayats tried **petty civil and criminal cases**.
**G.R. Rajagopalan (1962)** studied Nyaya Panchayats.
Examples: UP (**UP Panchayat Raj Act 1947**), Bihar's **Gram Kachahari**.

q.s:
Consider the following:

Reason (R): Under Article 243B, a State with a population not exceeding 20 lakh may not constitute Panchayats at the intermediate level.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false

q.s:
Assertion (A): The Gram Sabha is the village-level general assembly of all persons registered in the village electoral rolls.
Reason (R): The Gram Sabha is the elected executive body of the village.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
q.x: A is true: under Article 243(b) the Gram Sabha is the body of all persons registered as voters in the village electoral rolls. R is false: the elected executive body is the Gram Panchayat, not the Gram Sabha.
q.tq: Discriminate the Gram Sabha (all voters) from the Gram Panchayat (elected body).
n: The Gram Sabha is the village-level general assembly of all persons registered in the village electoral rolls. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The Gram Panchayat is the elected executive body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The Gram Sabha is the entire electorate of a village. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The Gram Sabha is the body of registered voters of a village. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]

q.s:

q.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: at least four-fifths, not all, of DPC members are elected.

q.s: When did the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965 come into force?
q.x: The Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965 has been in force from 2 April 1965.

It governs **Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats**.

**Third Amendment Bill 2026** adds a **Uniform Mutation Fee**, since neither the 1965 Act nor the 1955 Act allowed one.

q.s:

Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

o: Best interests of the child through child-friendly and rehabilitation-oriented justice
Detention in every case until adulthood
Retributive punishment as the primary objective

why: inclusive growth not from high growth alone

q.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Inclusive growth is not expected to come from a high growth rate of national income by itself.
Reason (R): Inclusive growth needs rural development, agricultural revival and adequate credit to farmers so that the poor participate in growth.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

q.s: Which one of the following statements about the 2010 MPI design is NOT correct?
o: It measures only extreme poverty below one dollar a day.
It considers multiple deprivations at the individual level.
It uses dimensions such as education, health and standard of living.
q.x: The MPI is not a measure restricted to extreme poverty below one dollar a day. It captures multiple deprivations across several dimensions.
q.tq: Reject an over-specific income-poverty description in favour of the multidimensional method.
xs: "**It measures only extreme poverty below one dollar a day**" is NOT correct — so option **(1)** is the answer (UPPSC 2025 trap).
The MPI does consider **multiple deprivations at the individual level**, uses **household-survey micro-data**, and covers **education, health and standard of living**.
xa: MPI = **headcount ratio × intensity**.
MPI-poor = deprived in at least **one-third** of weighted indicators.
Global MPI **developed in 2010**, replacing the HPI.

q.s:

Reason (R): It was proclaimed by the UN General Assembly in December 1991.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

q.s:
Consider the following statements:

Reason (R): Carrying capacity requires that extraction is not above the rate of regeneration and that wastes are within the assimilating capacity of the environment.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

q.s: What is unemployment caused by depression in an economy called?
q.x: A fall in aggregate demand during recession or depression causes cyclical unemployment (APPSC 2019).

Urban functions expanding along transport routes

q.x: Gilt-edged trading of existing securities is a secondary-market activity; the primary (new issue) market deals in new securities.

why: VAT does not reduce revenue buoyancy
